reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify baseline patterns across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This approach ensures both intuitive insight and data-driven validation of shared spurious features, especially when ground truth labels are missing and semantic relevance is uncertain.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features appear in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 11553)
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., education-num, age, workclass) has a semantically plausible link to income classification, or if it exists only as a statistical artifact
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justified conclusion on whether the shared feature is semantically relevant or spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP and integrated gradients provide global feature attributions, revealing which features drive predictions despite being semantically unrelated. LIME offers local interpretability to confirm feature impact in individual misclassifications. Sensitivity analysis quantifies how prediction changes when a feature is zeroed, identifying spurious dependencies. Together, these tools validate the autonomous findings and detect shared spurious patterns that might otherwise go unnoticed.
